narrative:
Three lenses produced twenty-four candidates. Merging them was mostly the work of noticing that the same garment had been named three times. Nine of the twenty-four collapsed into two ideas: an outdoor short that Nike already ships but nobody can find, and a rules-legal team bottoms system that a 2025-26 NFHS rule change made orderable for the first time. What survived is eight opportunities, and the merge itself is the finding - where three independent lenses converged, they converged on capture and architecture, not on invention.

How I clustered. First I merged by consumer-and-product, not by name. C-CONVERGENCE-4 (Outdoor Court, Found Not Invented), C-NONOBVIOUS-7 (Legible Function) and C-WHITESPACE-4 (Found Outdoors) are one move seen from three angles: an existing SKU (Nike DNA 6" UV Woven) that closes the UV, storage and abrasion gaps four domains independently declared open (A03-S7, A06-S4, A06-S7, A07-S8), failing not on capability but on legibility in a channel that is swinging to wholesale racks with no product copy (A02-S7). I then folded C-CONVERGENCE-5 (Trapped-Sweat Spec) and C-NONOBVIOUS-2 (Wet-State Spec) into it rather than keeping them separate: they name the same consumer and the same garment, and they are best read as the proof point that makes the franchise defensible - certify UPF, dry-time and dimensional stability at the 0.00-1.33 kg of sweat a basketball uniform actually traps (A06-S2), because untreated polyester already rates UPF 40-50 dry (A06-S7). That is OPP-02.

Second, the competition cluster. C-NONOBVIOUS-1 and C-WHITESPACE-2 are the same idea under the same name; C-CONVERGENCE-2 (Layer-Ready Court Short) is the core garment inside it. All three rest on the only genuinely new, dated, primary evidence in the base: NFHS Rule 3-4-5 permitting teammates to wear multiple styles of like-coloured bottoms, and FIBA's interpretation legalising compression undershorts at any length with team colour match (A06-S3). That becomes OPP-01. C-CONVERGENCE-1 (Two Books, One Block) was absorbed rather than kept - as written it targets both the competition and the free-play user at once, which fails the distinctness rule, but its architecture logic is preserved as pattern P-01 and inside OPP-01 and OPP-03.

Third, the unglamorous cluster. C-CONVERGENCE-6, C-NONOBVIOUS-4 and C-WHITESPACE-7 all point at the core men's franchise from different sides - a 67% recommend rate across 64 reviews (A04-S6), seams and shrinkage rather than pockets as the reproducible defect (A01-S3), and a liner three disciplines want deleted (A06-S6, A06-S3, A06-S2). Merged as OPP-03, with liner deletion as the funding mechanism for the seam and shrink fix, not as a separate product.

Geography merged cleanly: three Australia candidates became OPP-04, and Europe stood alone as OPP-05 because no other lens looked at it. The three event candidates became OPP-06. The two women's clusters stayed separate because they are genuinely different consumers: OPP-07 is the fan-and-day-wear lower half in fan doors, OPP-08 is the extended-size and long-inseam performance tier that the ladder currently prices as its basement.

What I dropped. C-CONVERGENCE-3 (Women's Length and Rise System) goes, as a standalone: its premise is the empty-women's-category claim the skeptics rejected three separate times (A01-O2, A02-O2, A05-O1), and Nike ships 5", 6.5", 7" and 9" women's bottoms plus Aero-FIT on a women's signature short first. Its residue - waist control on hip-first sizing (A06-S9), coverage, extended sizes - is carried in OPP-08 and OPP-01. I stripped the Aerogami reactive-vent feature from OPP-02 (three years, one jacket - a feasibility signal, not white space), the collab-and-resale premise from OPP-06 (A05-S10 is catalogue pages, not a resale market), the CunBA cultural anchor entirely (2023 evidence, inflating retellings, Li-Ning already activated), and the shoe-is-dead-so-the-short-is-the-entry-point logic from every thesis, because A01-S6 traces to one Substack post that Circana's own releases contradict.

Two contradictions travel forward unaveraged, because they are not resolvable here: inseam direction (A02-S5 against A07-S4), and Greater China as value tier or premium (A01-S7 against A02-S3 and A04-S2). And one caveat governs all eight: no shorts-level unit, price or sell-through data exists in this base in any geography. No price in this portfolio is anchored to a retrieved page. None of these should be read as a price recommendation.

cross_domain_patterns.title: Rules, biomechanics, consumer complaint and channel economics all say this is two products merchandised as one
cross_domain_patterns.description: Four evidence pools with nothing in common converge on a line-architecture conclusion no single domain stated. Primary rulebooks require competition shorts to clear the knee and permit colour-matched compression at any length (A06-S3, A06-S6). Peer-reviewed biomechanics says fit must be validated in a lateral defensive stance and at jump-landing hip flexion, where hem and waistband bind, with activity changing every 2-4 seconds (A06-S1). Consumer and product evidence says storage is the headline feature of the free-play short and simultaneously its most resented element (A01-S3, A06-S4, A07-S8, A03-S7). Commercial evidence says the competition garment is bought through a bookings-led, low-markdown dealer channel while the free-play garment lands on a promotional wholesale floor (A04-S9, A04-S4, A02-S7). The single basketball short sold to both worlds is the root structural error; one graded block expressed as two explicitly different families is the cheapest correction. Caveat: this does not settle inseam direction, which stays contested (A02-S5 against A07-S4).

cross_domain_patterns.title: The problem is capture, not invention - and seven researchers failing to find a shipped SKU is the measurement
cross_domain_patterns.description: A03, A06 and A07 each independently concluded that outdoor function, secure storage and UPF were unowned white space; one live inline SKU carrying UVA/UVB protection, side pockets, a phone-secure zip pocket and an abrasion claim closes all three at once (A03-S7, A06-S4, A06-S7, A07-S8). That is one un-run catalogue query counted three times, not three findings. But the surrounding evidence for a capture problem is genuinely multi-pool: Nike apparel grows on price and mix with units up 1% (A03-S9); the volume franchise sits at 3.9 stars with 67% recommending on a real sample while the step-up clears at roughly 25% off (A04-S6); Nike Digital has fallen for ten consecutive quarters while wholesale grew (A02-S7); teen apparel mindshare trails footwear mindshare by twenty points and is still falling among girls (A01-S1); Greater China apparel units fell 8% against growing participation (A04-S2). Competitors win the same shelf by printing function and place on the outside of the garment (A07-S9, A03-S7). Legibility, not capability, is the gap.

cross_domain_patterns.title: The rulebook is the only dataset in the base that actually changed, and it changed toward women, layering and the team channel
cross_domain_patterns.description: Across the surviving signals almost everything is stable, stale or contested. Exactly two items are new, dated, primary and verified: NFHS Rule 3-4-5 for 2025-26 permitting teammates to wear multiple STYLES of like-coloured uniform bottoms so religious and personal accommodations no longer require a permission request, and FIBA's official interpretation that compression undershorts are legal at ANY length provided the team matches colour. Both sit inside A06-S3 and both were surfaced by the skeptic rather than the specialist. The non-obvious step is commercial, not technical: team bottoms are ordered by coaches through dealers against a compliance spec (A04-S9), so a rule that widens what counts as compliant is what makes a non-standard bottom orderable as stock at all. Three needs argued elsewhere from far weaker evidence converge on that opening - coverage-first and modest-dress players (A05-S8), the layering population (A06-S6), and women sized hip-first with an under-controlled waist (A06-S9) - and it lands on the consumer where Nike's mindshare erosion is concentrated (A01-S1).

cross_domain_patterns.title: The garment is specified dry and used wet; every unresolved failure mode lives in the saturated state
cross_domain_patterns.description: Read across disciplines, the failure modes cluster in one physical condition nobody tested. Basketball uniforms trap 0.00-1.33 kg of sweat, rising with intensity and with a wider range than treadmill running (A06-S2). Peer-reviewed testing shows 100% polyester technical sportswear already rates UPF 40-50+ untreated - but that is a dry rating, and the open variable is what moisture does to it (A06-S7). Drawstrings slip when saturated and the waist is left to the drawcord on hip-first women's sizing (A06-S9). The reproducible consumer complaints are seam failure and shrinkage after a single wash, which is a post-wet-state defect (A01-S3, A01-S2, A04-S6). The priority use case is 27-32C humid outdoor play (A06-S5). So the entire spec conversation - GSM, UPF, abrasion, dry time - is conducted on a dry garment while the entire consumer conversation is about a soaked one. Invisible to any single specialist because the sweat number sits in sports science, UV degradation in textile chemistry, seam failure in retail reviews and humidity in climate data.

cross_domain_patterns.title: Women's demand survives deduplication on four independent instruments; the empty-category premise does not
cross_domain_patterns.description: The WNBA 2024 press release is one document that reached three domains and must count once. What remains is independent and still points one way: Unrivaled's verified operations - ticket revenue +204%, tickets +249%, a professional women's record crowd, and one Philadelphia night generating roughly USD 1M in tickets and USD 400,000 in merchandise (A05-S7); Australia's national participation registry showing female participation +25% since 2022 past 450,000, unconnected to any US league (A02-S9); a retailer CEO stating on his own call that basketball is coming back built around women's basketball and that boys and girls are both buying it (A04-S5); and a US teen survey showing Nike's female mindshare still declining (A01-S1). Four unrelated instruments, one direction. The same pattern kills the product premise attached to it: Nike ships ISoFly, Crossover, Fly Crossover, WNBA Victory and Rebel Fanwear shorts and Sabrina, and put Aero-FIT on a women's signature short first (A03-S6, A03-S4). The unserved job is the lower half of the fan wardrobe and a waist-and-coverage system - not an absent category.

cross_domain_patterns.title: The portfolio is weighted inversely to the quality of its own evidence
cross_domain_patterns.description: Ranking the surviving base by evidence quality rather than by stated priority inverts the portfolio. Australia is the best-verified non-US signal in the file - roughly 1.3M players, second among team participation sports, female participation +25% past 450,000, an estimated 150,000 players turned away for lack of court space, NBL attendance above 1.2M with 58-63 sellouts, and an on-court league partner that is not a performance-basketball leader (A02-S9, A05-S6) - and every skeptic correction ran in its favour. It supports one signal and no opportunity. Greater China carries the largest share of the portfolio on evidence sourced almost entirely from outside China, in Nike's worst-performing region: revenue -13% currency-neutral with apparel units -8% (A02-S2, A04-S2), Li-Ning basketball retail sales -19% amid discounting (A02-S3) with an unresolved conflict against +5% in H1 2026 (A04-S2), and e-commerce leadership flipped (A04-S11). Europe, Nike's second geography, is the primary market of zero signals and appears only as a stripped CAGR, a markdown line and a compliance deadline (A02-S1, A04-S4, A03-S5). No single specialist could see this; it appears only when the seven files are counted together.

cross_domain_patterns.title: Full-price demand concentrates where people physically gather, while the promotional floor sits where product is planned - and a competitor proved the mechanism in another sport
cross_domain_patterns.description: Two datasets that never meet say the same thing. Commercially, the US wholesale marketplace turned increasingly promotional with Foot Locker comps -3.6% and Nike citing elevated markdowns (A04-S4), and Nike's ASP gain is mix rather than pricing power, already partly eroded by discounts (A03-S9). Culturally, the live economy is doing the opposite: Unrivaled's Philadelphia night produced roughly USD 1M in tickets and USD 400,000 in merchandise while broadcast viewership fell 9% (A05-S7); the NBL ran a third consecutive million-plus season with 58-63 sellouts (A05-S6, A02-S9); streetball moved into stadium venues. The mechanism at scale is proven inside this base by a rival's own disclosure - adidas apparel +35% currency-neutral in a quarter on World Cup demand while its basketball fell 21% (A04-S3). Channel evidence says the resulting product must travel through wholesale and in-arena rather than as app drops (A02-S7). The SS28 calendar that would anchor this appears in none of the seven files, and the scale calibration must travel with the claim: most of these moments are small in absolute terms.

cross_domain_patterns.title: The price ladder is inverted against three under-served consumers at once: coverage is priced as cheapness
cross_domain_patterns.description: The longest, most size-inclusive SKU in the men's line - the DNA Academy 11-inch, Big and Tall included - is also the cheapest at roughly USD 37, while the 6-inch sits at USD 65 and the 10-inch discounts around 38% (A02-S4, A02-S5). That single architectural fact collides with three findings none of which was read next to it: the coverage-first need among taller women and modest-dressing athletes (A05-S8), plus-size and value replenishment behaviour where AND1 runs to 5XL and is called affordable and cultural (A01-S9), and the retro lifestyle pole defined as 9 inches or longer (A05-S3). Women's plus exists only as a single SKU inside a signature line (A03-S6), and the waist on hip-first women's sizing is left to a drawcord (A06-S9). So the length three under-served groups want is the line's basement product, in the cheapest fabric, with no women's grading. Meanwhile the floor beneath is rising rather than falling under a roughly 53.5% duty stack (A04-S8). Inseam data sits in marketplace, modesty in culture, plus-size in consumer and price in commercial, so nobody plotted the line.

cross_domain_patterns.title: The short is a top layer in a system, the sewn-in liner is the component three disciplines want deleted, and deleting it funds the fix a fourth demands
cross_domain_patterns.description: Independently, athlete, product and culture each described a garment worn over something else without naming the system. FIBA permits compression undershorts at any length with team colour matching, and the 2025-26 NFHS change permits multiple like-coloured bottom styles (A06-S3). Biomechanics explains why the interface matters: activity changes every 2-4 seconds across roughly 450 lateral movements and 42-56 jumps, so a waistband sliding on slick compression is a repeated failure (A06-S1). Women's hip-first sizing leaves the waist to a drawstring that slips when saturated (A06-S9, A06-S2). A regional convention already ships the answer commercially - Philippine team practice pairs a compression liner with a loose short (A03-S10) - and coverage-first players solve it with short-over-legging (A05-S8). Commercially the liner is the densest fabric mass in a garment that traps up to 1.33 kg of sweat, in a use case that is 27-32C and humid (A06-S5), on a franchise drawing seam and paper-thin complaints at a price point with limited headroom (A04-S6, A01-S3, A04-S8). Deleting a component two groups do not want funds the construction the third is complaining about. The binding unknown is prevalence: layering rates below elite level are entirely unmeasured (A06-S6).

cross_domain_patterns.title: Every Western competitor is retreating from performance basketball apparel exactly as wholesale becomes Nike's growth channel
cross_domain_patterns.description: adidas basketball fell 21% in the quarter, Under Armour is separating from Curry with apparel available only through October 2026, and Puma's basketball growth is a residual with basketball absent from its stated priorities (A04-S3, A02-S8). The one riser is New Balance: +19% to USD 9.2B, apparel past USD 1B, 80 new doors, Cooper Flagg signed, and a 7-inch mesh basketball short already in Foot Locker (A02-S8). Simultaneously Nike's own channel mix inverted - wholesale +4% while Nike Digital declined for a tenth consecutive quarter (A02-S7, A04-S1). Physical shelf is opening in the doors that are growing, and in Australia the league's on-court partner is not a performance-basketball brand (A02-S9). Two countervailing facts must travel with this: the freed space is small in absolute dollars, and the doors it opens in are promotional (A04-S4). It is a share-of-shelf and full-price-productivity opportunity, not a category-growth one, and Nike's own basketball growth is footwear-weighted with no basketball-apparel disclosure anywhere (A04-S1).

cross_domain_patterns.title: Heat is the only functional need corroborated by physiology, institutional behaviour change and a competitor's multi-year platform commitment
cross_domain_patterns.description: Three unrelated pools point at thermal load in outdoor basketball. Peer-reviewed measurement supplies the only garment-level number in the entire base: basketball uniforms trap 0.00-1.33 kg of sweat, rising with intensity (A06-S2). Institutional behaviour change documents the consequence independently in the Philippines, where athletic meets moved away from 9am-3pm from 2024 and one 2024 provincial meet recorded more heat-related than sports-related injuries (A06-S5). Competitor commitment corroborates commercially: Li-Ning's Wade UPF 50+ / AT Dry platform runs across consistent style codes from Spring 2023 through 2025 at a price far below Nike's, and nike.com.cn already runs an outdoor section (A03-S7). Nike's own innovation direction agrees - cooling is its declared apparel vector and has now shipped into basketball (A03-S4). No two of these share a source. What none establishes is price, or that Nike's existing polyester does not already deliver the UPF claim dry (A06-S7), and every sweat measurement in hand is from air-conditioned North American gyms while the target play is hot and humid.

opportunities.name: Like-Colored
opportunities.thesis: Sell a rules-legal team BOTTOMS SYSTEM rather than a better team short: a knee-clearing linerless game short, a longer bottom and colour-matched 3/4 and full-length compression, orderable together in team colours with compliant logo placement. The 2025-26 NFHS Rule 3-4-5 change permitting teammates to wear multiple STYLES of like-coloured bottoms, plus FIBA's interpretation legalising compression undershorts at any length with team colour matching (A06-S3), converts coverage, modesty and layering from per-athlete permission requests into an orderable stock SKU family - and it routes through the one channel in this base that is bookings-led and low-markdown rather than promotional (A04-S9). HYPOTHESIS, not finding: no one has counted how many programmes would order a mixed set.
opportunities.intersection: Federation and state-association rulebooks x team-dealer B2B channel economics x women's, modest-dress and layering fit needs x biomechanics of the waistband interface
opportunities.target_consumer: US high-school and club/AAU programme buyers - coaches and athletic directors ordering rosters through BSN and peer dealers - and through them the athletes the rule was written for: girls' and women's teams, coverage-first and modest-dressing players, and the population already wearing 3/4 tights under a game short. Secondary: Australian club programmes where female participation is up 25% since 2022 (A02-S9).
opportunities.why_hard_to_see: The trigger is a single line in an NFHS rules-change release - a document apparel PLMs do not read, and one the athlete specialist missed by using a diocesan PDF as a proxy; it survives in this base only as skeptic counter-evidence inside A06-S3. The channel fact sits in a commercial signal (A04-S9) that contains no basketball-shorts data at all. The human need sits in a culture signal built on 2014-2017 evidence (A05-S8). Each of the three needs was argued elsewhere from much weaker evidence - a 2014 quote, an SEO compression guide, a sizing boilerplate sentence - so the strong version was never assembled. And it is an assortment architecture rather than a hero product, so it produces no image for a line review.
opportunities.distinctness_note: Distinct from OPP-03 (which is the men's core wholesale franchise and its make quality) and from OPP-08 (which is a consumer-retail extended-size and long-inseam tier). This one is defined by a compliance spec, a roster order and a dealer channel; its buyer is a coach, not a shopper. It absorbs C-CONVERGENCE-2 (the linerless layer-ready short is the core garment of this system) and the competition half of C-CONVERGENCE-1. It deliberately does NOT claim a women's category gap - the rejected A01-O2, A02-O2 and A05-O1 all did, and Nike ships 5", 6.5", 7" and 9" women's bottoms.

opportunities.name: Found Outdoors
opportunities.thesis: Nike already ships a basketball short with UVA/UVB protection, side pockets, a phone-secure zip pocket and a rebound-battle durability claim, and four domains independently declared all of that unowned white space (A03-S7, A06-S4, A06-S7, A07-S8). So the outdoor opportunity is not to invent - it is to name a franchise, extend it beyond one inseam, take it into the hot-climate markets where the competitive price is actually set, make its function legible on a wholesale rack with no product copy (A02-S7, A07-S9), and give it the one proof point nobody in the category has: UPF, dry-time and dimensional stability certified in the SATURATED state, against the 0.00-1.33 kg of sweat a basketball uniform actually traps (A06-S2), because untreated polyester already rates UPF 40-50 dry (A06-S7).
opportunities.intersection: An existing but unfindable SKU x sweat physiology x textile UV chemistry x hot-climate institutional behaviour change x the wholesale channel swing
opportunities.target_consumer: Outdoor and half-court players 15-35 on concrete, asphalt and acrylic in hot markets - Greater China lower-tier cities, the Philippines, Southeast Asia, India, the US Sun Belt, Australia and the Gulf - who play multi-hour sessions, are soaked inside the first game, carry a phone and keys with no locker, and currently default to Li-Ning Wade UPF or Anta quick-dry product.
opportunities.why_hard_to_see: It presents as a merchandising failure, so no product owner claims it: three domains looked at the same shipped SKU and wrote it up as a gap, which pushes the organisation toward inventing rather than distributing. The failure of seven researchers to find a product they had no trouble finding at Li-Ning is itself the data, and no researcher can observe their own blind spot. The genuinely open technical question sits between two literatures that never cite each other - a physiology paper measuring trapped sweat, and a textile paper saying polyester is already UPF 40-50 dry and that moisture is the untested variable - so read separately they are two reasons NOT to build a product, and only together do they say the category's sun claim is measured in a state the player is never in.
opportunities.distinctness_note: Merges C-CONVERGENCE-4, C-NONOBVIOUS-7 and C-WHITESPACE-4 (three names for one move) and absorbs C-CONVERGENCE-5 and C-NONOBVIOUS-2 (the wet-state spec), which target the same consumer with the same garment and are therefore its proof point, not a second opportunity. Distinct from OPP-04, which is a market-sequencing decision about where this lands first. The Aerogami reactive-vent feature is deliberately excluded: three years and one jacket reads as a feasibility signal, not white space (A07-S2).

opportunities.name: Twenty Washes
opportunities.thesis: The highest-certainty margin and trust return in this portfolio is not a new short: it is fixing seam construction and post-wash dimensional stability on the franchise that carries the units, and funding it by deleting the sewn-in brief liner that three separate disciplines want removed. The reproducible complaints are seams and shrinkage after one wash, not pockets (A01-S3, A04-S6); the volume franchise sits at 3.9 stars with 67% recommending across 64 reviews (A04-S6); apparel growth is price-and-mix led with units up 1% (A03-S9); and the liner is redundant for players who layer compression - explicitly rules-legal at any length (A06-S3, A06-S6) - and is the densest wet mass in a garment that traps up to 1.33 kg of sweat (A06-S2). Own durability as the one premium claim nobody at premium makes.
opportunities.intersection: Retail review corpora x markdown and margin structure x the composition of ASP growth x elite layering behaviour and FIBA rules x sweat-trapping garment physiology
opportunities.target_consumer: Men and boys 16-35 buying core Nike basketball shorts (Icon, DNA) at Dick's, Foot Locker, Walmart, Kohl's, JD and Amazon in North America and EMEA - the largest single unit pool in the category and the one Nike already owns - plus the parents replenishing for them, and the competitive player who wears tights underneath and gets nothing from a second brief.
opportunities.why_hard_to_see: The four inputs are owned by four functions that do not meet: review sentiment with consumer experience, markdown depth with sales, fabric GSM history with materials, and the composition of ASP growth with finance. Each alone looks like noise. The failure mode was also mis-diagnosed inside the base - the consumer domain built a pocket-engineering recommendation on one unverified snippet while the same review corpus reproducibly complains about seams and shrinkage - and the one usable quality datapoint (67% recommend across 64 reviews) was found by a skeptic, not a specialist. Nobody costed the liner, and nobody noticed that the physiological, competitive-rules and P&L arguments for deleting it point at the same component from three unconnected files. It is also the least exciting candidate here, which is why no domain led with it.
opportunities.distinctness_note: Merges C-CONVERGENCE-6, C-NONOBVIOUS-4 and C-WHITESPACE-7. Distinct from OPP-01 (team channel, compliance spec, roster order) and OPP-08 (extended sizes and long inseam at a new tier): this is the existing core men's wholesale franchise at its existing price, changed on make rather than on assortment. Critical caveat carried forward: nobody has established that fabric GSM ever changed, and the sub-USD-100 price freeze that supposedly forced a cost-down has been superseded by roughly 3% apparel price increases (A04-S8) - so the premise may be false and the fix expensive.

opportunities.name: Southern Court
opportunities.thesis: Land the Worldball product where the evidence is strongest rather than where the priority space points. Australia is the only market in this base with registry-grade participation growth (roughly 1.3M players, second among team sports, female participation +25% since 2022 past 450,000, an estimated 150,000 turned away for lack of court space), a league at real scale with 58-63 sellouts, an on-court partner that is not a performance-basketball leader, doors Nike already sells through, and an established consumer literacy for UPF that makes it the right first market for OPP-02's wet-state proof (A02-S9, A05-S6, A06-S7, A02-S7). Every skeptic correction ran in this signal's favour. Frame it honestly as a proving ground that generates the sell-through dataset this entire evidence base lacks - not as a volume market.
opportunities.intersection: A national participation registry x verified league operations x competitor retreat from performance basketball x a national sun-protection standard and consumer literacy
opportunities.target_consumer: Australian players 14-30, disproportionately the female cohort that has grown 25% since 2022 past 450,000 on the back of She Hoops, plus club and school players inside a roughly 1.3M-player base, buying through Rebel, JD and Foot Locker Australia, with NBL fandom as the cultural surround.
opportunities.why_hard_to_see: Portfolio attention follows the stated priority space, and no specialist compares evidence QUALITY across geographies - each reports what its own searches returned. It takes counting the base by primary geography and by source provenance to see that roughly three quarters is US-derived, that the China narrative is assembled almost entirely from non-Chinese sources with no retrieved Chinese price anywhere, and that the single best-verified non-US market supports one signal and no opportunity. Australia is also a small line inside APLA that never generates a global brief, and the detail that makes the case - 150,000 players turned away, female participation past 450,000 - surfaced only in a skeptic's correction.
opportunities.distinctness_note: This is a market-sequencing and go-to-market opportunity, not a second outdoor product: the garment is OPP-02's, and the argument is about where it lands first and what it proves. Distinct from OPP-05 (Europe) by market, consumer, doors and rationale - Australia is chosen for evidence quality, Europe for scale and neglect. Deliberately does not deprioritise Greater China as a market; it argues about the order of proof, and the contradiction with the stated SS28 priority space (A01-S7) is preserved rather than resolved.

opportunities.name: Continental
opportunities.thesis: Europe is Nike's second geography and the primary market of exactly zero signals in this base - it enters the analysis only as a compliance deadline, a markdown line, a set of doors and a discount channel where Li-Ning's sustained Wade UPF 50+ platform already clears at roughly EUR 20 (A02-S1, A04-S4, A02-S7, A03-S7). A Europe-first basketball shorts programme built to a substantiated-claims standard that the EU Empowering Consumers Directive rewards rather than punishes (A03-S5), sold through the doors that already carry basketball streetwear (KICKZ, Zalando, club retail), turns a compliance burden into a claim advantage in the one region where a challenger has just proved the market responds (New Balance +30% in Europe, A02-S8). Explicitly a research-gated opportunity: it is currently unfalsifiable and must not be sized before a minimum viable European read.
opportunities.intersection: An unexamined geography with live doors x incoming claims regulation x a Chinese value platform already retailing in Europe x challenger proof that the region responds
opportunities.target_consumer: European club, school and pickup players 15-30 in Germany, Spain, Greece, Turkey, Lithuania and Serbia, plus the specialty streetwear buyer already shopping KICKZ and Zalando; secondarily the European value buyer currently picking up discounted Li-Ning Wade product at around EUR 20.
opportunities.why_hard_to_see: A PLM in Beaverton sees Europe as an execution region, not a creation region, so it never generates a brief - and every research input here is US-derived, which reproduces the blind spot rather than correcting it. Europe also enters the file only as negatives (a -24% digital number and a regulation), which reads as a reason to avoid rather than to build. The single strongest European fact in the base - that a Chinese competitor's sustained outdoor platform is already clearing at EUR 20 through European resellers - is filed inside a signal about Greater China (A03-S7), where no one looking at Europe would find it.
opportunities.distinctness_note: The only candidate no other lens produced. Distinct from OPP-04 by market, doors and rationale: Australia is chosen because the evidence is strong, Europe because the evidence is absent and the scale is not. It carries a research gate rather than a product claim - unlike every other opportunity here, its first deliverable is a market read (EuroLeague/Basketball England/DBB participation plus KICKZ and Zalando sell-through), not a garment.

opportunities.name: Doha to LA
opportunities.thesis: The only proven antidote in this base to a promotional apparel floor is a dated moment: adidas grew apparel 35% currency-neutral in one quarter on World Cup demand in the very quarter its basketball fell 21% (A04-S3), while the US marketplace Nike sells shorts into turned increasingly promotional (A04-S4) and Nike's ASP gain is mix rather than pricing power (A03-S9). The SS28 window contains the two largest basketball moments of the cycle and not one of seven specialist files mentions either. A moment-anchored, shorts-first programme sold through wholesale and in-arena - the channels that are actually growing (A02-S7) - is the one way a basketball short gets a full-price reason to exist. Sized honestly to attendance, not to narrative: the largest continental property in this base drew roughly nine NBL games' worth of people across a whole season (A05-S6).
opportunities.intersection: A competitor's football-quarter financials x the promotional floor in US wholesale x verified live-event and streetball operations x heat physiology in a market with no evidence in the base
opportunities.target_consumer: Fan-and-player crossover buyers 14-34 around national-team and streetball moments - US buyers around a home Games, European, Asian and Gulf federation followers around a world championship, and event attendees buying on site where full price demonstrably holds (roughly USD 400,000 of merchandise in one Unrivaled night, A05-S7).
opportunities.why_hard_to_see: PLM calendars run on seasons; federation calendars run on qualification cycles, and nobody owns the join - which is why the SS28 calendar is absent from all seven files and had to be supplied by the cross-dataset audit. Worse, the proof of the mechanism was sitting inside the commercial file as a competitor datapoint about FOOTBALL, filed under 'competitors are retreating from basketball', so the one number showing how to beat a promotional floor was read as evidence of a rival's weakness. A basketball PLM has no reason to read adidas's football quarter; a commercial analyst had no reason to read it as a calendar instruction.
opportunities.distinctness_note: Merges C-CONVERGENCE-8, C-NONOBVIOUS-8 and C-WHITESPACE-3. Distinct from OPP-07 (a standing women's fan assortment, not a dated capsule) and from OPP-02 (an inline outdoor franchise, not a moment). Two deliberate strippings: the collab-and-resale premise is removed because every citation behind it is a catalogue or product page with no price, premium or volume data (A05-S10), and the anchoring calendar facts come from the audit rather than from any surviving signal - they must be confirmed before anything is planned against them.

opportunities.name: The Other Half
opportunities.thesis: Women's basketball demand is real and now durable across three seasons on four independent instruments (A05-S7, A02-S9, A04-S5, A01-S1), and it is converting into TOPS: the strongest search term in the base is 'female jersey outfit' at +494% (A05-S4), the supply chain is jersey-led (A05-S1), and Sabrina reviewers report wearing the short at home more than on court (A03-S6). The unserved job is therefore not a missing women's category - Nike ships ISoFly, Crossover, Fly Crossover, Sabrina, WNBA Victory and Rebel Fanwear shorts - it is a women's-BLOCK lower half designed and merchandised as the other half of a jersey outfit, in fan and event doors rather than on the performance wall. HYPOTHESIS: the cheapest test in the entire portfolio is splitting the Unrivaled Philadelphia USD 400,000 merchandise night by category.
opportunities.intersection: Platform search-and-save behaviour x live-event merchandise economics x a first-party retailer demand call-out x a performance SKU's actual reported use occasion
opportunities.target_consumer: Women and girls 16-35 in the US who follow the WNBA, Unrivaled and NCAA and dress the fandom daily - and, per Ed Stack's own words on his call, the cross-gender buyer: 'boys and girls, young men and women are buying that product' (A04-S5). Bought in fan doors and at events, not on the performance wall.
opportunities.why_hard_to_see: It requires reading the Pinterest data AGAINST the inference the culture domain drew from it: A05 used jersey-search growth as proof that consumers want shorts, when the strongest term argues for tops. The correct reading only appears next to a product-domain finding buried in skeptic counter-evidence - that Sabrina buyers wear the short at home, so the USD 65 willingness-to-pay is lifestyle-driven - and next to an event-retail number the culture specialist missed. Three files each held a third of it and each drew a performance conclusion. Three domains also read the same 2024 WNBA press release and concluded the category was empty, which is false, so the correct move (retarget the occasion) looks identical to the incorrect one (create the category) and gets rejected on audit.
opportunities.distinctness_note: Merges C-NONOBVIOUS-5 and C-WHITESPACE-6. Deliberately narrower than the rejected A05-O4 and A01-O2: it does NOT claim a team-identity fan short is missing - Nike shipped the WNBA Rebel Fanwear short in May 2026 - and it does not propose a new women's inseam ladder. The claim is about block, proportion, rise and merchandising adjacency to the jersey. Distinct from OPP-01 (competition roster order through dealers) and OPP-08 (extended sizes and long inseam as a performance tier). Carry the pan-sport contradiction openly: F1 aesthetic +483% and Brazil jersey outfit women +302% grow as fast or faster, so the basketball attribution is not supported by A05-S4.

opportunities.name: Full Range
opportunities.thesis: Break the ladder inversion. Nike's longest, most size-inclusive short - the DNA Academy 11-inch including Big and Tall - is also its cheapest at roughly USD 37, while the 6-inch sits at USD 65 and the 10-inch discounts around 38% (A02-S4, A02-S5), which prices coverage as cheapness for the three groups that most want it: coverage-first and modest-dressing players (A05-S8), plus and big-and-tall players currently choosing AND1 to 5XL as 'affordable and cultural' (A01-S9), and the retro buyer for whom 9 inches or longer is the defining spec (A05-S3). Build a properly constructed long tier in heavier mesh with women's grading, real waist control on hip-first sizing (A06-S9) and extended sizes offered at the TOP of the range rather than only at the bottom. The competitors holding this space are value brands and a licensed heritage label, and the duty stack is weakening them (A04-S8).
opportunities.intersection: Inseam price architecture x coverage-first and modest-dress need x plus-size and value replenishment behaviour x women's hip-first sizing and waist control
opportunities.target_consumer: Three groups served today by the same USD 37 SKU or by value brands: taller, longer-legged and modest-dressing women who need real coverage; plus, tall and big-and-tall players buying AND1 to 5XL or Mitchell & Ness at DXL; and the big-and-tall retro buyer. Bought in the wholesale and extended-size doors that are growing (A02-S7).
opportunities.why_hard_to_see: Size extension is treated as a size-curve decision made after the line is set, not as a whitespace with its own price and product logic, so it never surfaces as an opportunity. The four facts are each unremarkable alone and only the arrangement is interesting - and the decisive datapoint, 11 inches at USD 37 including Big and Tall, appears in this base only as skeptic counter-evidence used to REFUTE a 'design at the poles' recommendation, never to reveal a pricing inversion. The modesty need sits in a culture signal a decade stale, the plus-size behaviour in a consumer signal built on unranked listings, and no domain owns 'price by inseam' as a question, so nobody plotted the line.
opportunities.distinctness_note: Merges C-NONOBVIOUS-6 and C-WHITESPACE-8, and carries the surviving residue of C-CONVERGENCE-3 (waist control, coverage, extended sizes) without its rejected premise. Distinct from OPP-07 (fan and day-wear occasion in fan doors) and OPP-01 (roster compliance through dealers): this is a retail price-and-size architecture move on the performance wall. The inseam-direction contradiction sits directly underneath it and is NOT resolved here - A07-S4 argues the poles, A02-S5's own cited source says 7-9 inches, and Nike's live ladder runs 6-11 inches continuously, so unit share by inseam must be pulled before this is built.

dropped_candidates.reason: Women's Length and Rise System, dropped as a standalone opportunity. Its premise is the empty-women's-category claim the skeptics rejected three separate times (A01-O2, A02-O2 and A05-O1 are all in rejected.json for exactly this), and it is false: Nike ships Crossover 5", ISoFly 6.5" and 7", Seasonal 9", Fly Crossover, WNBA Victory and Rebel Fanwear shorts and Sabrina, and put Aero-FIT on a women's signature short first. Proposing a women's inseam ladder duplicates in-flight work weeks before the Caitlin Clark line reaches retail. The genuinely surviving residue - waist control on hip-first sizing (A06-S9), coverage length, extended sizes, and the rules change that makes mixed team bottoms orderable - is carried in OPP-08 and OPP-01, and the demand case is carried in OPP-07.

Two Books, One Block, absorbed rather than kept. As written it targets the competition user and the free-play user simultaneously with one architecture, which fails the distinctness rule and would have made every other opportunity a sub-case of it. Its logic is preserved as pattern PAT-01 and inside OPP-01 (the competition family), OPP-02 (the free-play family) and OPP-03 (the shared block and the liner decision).

Five candidates, one opportunity. Trapped-Sweat Spec and Wet-State Spec are the same idea (specify and certify in the saturated state) from two lenses; Outdoor Court Found Not Invented, Legible Function and Found Outdoors are the same move from three. All five name the same consumer and the same garment, so under the distinctness rule they are one: OPP-02, with the wet-state certification as its proof point rather than as a separate product.

Straight duplicate merges where two or three lenses produced the same opportunity under different names: Like-Colored / Layer-Ready (OPP-01), the make-quality and liner-deletion cluster (OPP-03), the three Australia candidates (OPP-04), the three event candidates (OPP-06), the two women's game-day candidates (OPP-07), and Coverage Tier / Full Range (OPP-08). In each case the sharper framing was kept and the weaker one's distinct evidence folded in.

The Aerogami reactive-vent feature is stripped from OPP-02 and appears in no thesis. It is a June 2023 technology that in three years has shipped on nothing but one Run Division jacket; three years of non-extension reads as a cost, abrasion or wash-durability signal, not as white space (A07-S2 classified hype). Separately, no opportunity claims Aero-FIT is missing from basketball - it shipped on the Sabrina 4 collection on 17 July 2026, which is why A07-S1 and A07-O1 were rejected - and no price in this portfolio is stated as a fact, since the entire retrieved price ladder failed audit.

No CunBA or village-basketball cultural anchor is carried into any opportunity. Every retrievable datapoint is 2023-2024, the viewership figure inflates from 100 million (Xinhua) to 800 million to 1 billion (CGTN) for the same event - evidence of amplification, not reach - and the space is already occupied by a funded Li-Ning athlete activation. A05-S5 is classified hype; building a 2028 line against a 2023 media peak fails the rule against resting on hype-classified signals.

Two framings excluded from every thesis. First, 'the basketball shoe is dead so the short is the lifestyle entry point' - A01-S6's Circana -11% and NPD 4%-share figures trace to a single Substack guest post that neither the skeptic nor the audit could reproduce, and Circana's own releases and Nike's FY26 disclosure point the other way. Second, the collab-and-resale premise (A05-S10, classified hype): every citation is a catalogue or product page with no price, premium-over-retail or sale-volume datapoint, so it cannot carry OPP-06 or any drop strategy. Both are available as research questions, not as reasons to build.
